fieldValues.title: relation create does not sync Part-container membership across a Part boundary
fieldValues.summary: record delete --cascade auto-removes a deleted instance from every Part container's declared memberInstanceIds, but relation create has no equivalent auto-add -- reparenting a leaf into a concept that lives under a different Part than its old parent silently drifts that Part's declared membership until fixed by hand via the CLI.
fieldValues.rationale:
Confirmed in srs#710/PR #758: reparenting 41 orphaned example leaves from 7 retiring subsection husks to their sibling mechanisms' concept parents (Protocol, Import tracking, Theme, Lifecycle, View, Repository) moved them out of the Extensions Part's contains-subtree and into four other Parts (Distribution, Structure, Foundations, Presentation) that actually reach those concepts. Nothing about `srs relation create --relation-type contains` touches any container file, so all 41 stayed declared under Extensions' old membership and were never added to the new Part's declared membership. `part-container-membership.mjs --check` (scripts/checks.json id part-container-membership, tier always, so it runs inside validate-all.mjs) caught this: validate-all.mjs went from exit 0 (verified against a pristine clone of the prior commit, not the local worktree -- a `git stash` without `-u` leaves untracked files in place and produced a false '4 containers already drifted at baseline' reading the first time this was checked) to exit 1 the moment the reparenting relations existed, and back to exit 0 only after every affected id was individually moved with `srs container members remove <old-part-container-id> <id>` / `srs container members add <new-part-container-id> <id>`.

The fix requires knowing which Part's contains-subtree the new parent concept actually lives under -- not assuming it's the same Part the old husk belonged to. Determine this by walking `contains` from each of the manifest's Part anchors (`manifest.json`'s `container.memberInstanceIds`, excluding `identityInstanceId`) and checking which one's subtree already reaches the target concept, before adding the reparented ids to that Part's container (found via the container file whose `anchorInstanceId` equals the Part concept's id, then use its own `containerId` -- not the anchor id -- as the `srs container members add/remove` argument).

This would change if `relation create` (or a future bulk contains-retarget verb, srs-rust#178's identity-preserving retype territory) grew Part-membership awareness of its own -- a `contains` edge fully determines the correct subtree membership already, so the sync is mechanical and does not need a human judgment call, only a missing piece of automation. Until then, any unit that reparents a `contains` edge across Part boundaries -- not just this section/subsection retirement series -- needs this same check.
